title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 203: The Revival of Acoustic Ecology
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 203 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Revival of Acoustic Ecology

Paragraph 1. For many years, wildlife scientists counted forest animals by looking for them with cameras, binoculars, or flying drones. However, seeing animals in thick jungles is very hard. Many creatures hide behind leaves, stay away from human smells, or only come out at night in the dark. Because of this problem, a new study called soundscape ecology listens to the sounds of nature instead of only taking pictures.

Paragraph 2. Scientists divide all forest sounds into three simple groups: animal sounds (like frogs and monkeys), natural weather sounds (like wind and thunder), and human machine noise. In a healthy forest, each animal species uses its own sound level and time so they do not shout over each other. When workers cut down trees, this quiet order breaks down.

Paragraph 3. To record forest sounds, scientists use small, cheap sound boxes called ARUs. Workers tie these boxes onto trees to record non-stop for months. Soon, a huge problem appeared: just twelve recorders in one park collected 30,000 hours of sound in a single season! A human listener would need decades to hear all those files. Today, smart computer programmes scan the recordings automatically. In Peru, Dr. Julian Rivera's software found illegal tree cutting within 48 hours, even though space satellites missed it under thick leaves.

Paragraph 4. Still, recording nature is not easy. Wet jungle air damages sensitive microphones. Also, heavy rain can hide quiet bird calls for days. Near cities, loud traffic noise covers up animal voices, making computers think the forest is empty when animals are really there.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q5.text: Cameras and drones can easily spot every animal living inside thick jungles.

steps: Đoạn 1: Động vật trốn sau lá cây hoặc ra vào ban đêm nên nhìn thấy chúng rất khó (very hard).

q6.text: Scientists separate forest sounds into three distinct groups.

steps: Đoạn 2: "Scientists divide all forest sounds into three simple groups..."

q7.text: Human workers can listen to 30,000 hours of forest audio in just one week.

steps: Đoạn 3: Con người phải mất hàng thập kỷ (need decades) chứ không thể nghe hết trong 1 tuần.

q8.text: Sound recording devices in jungles are frequently stolen by tourists.

steps: Đoạn 4: Chỉ nói không khí ẩm làm hỏng micro, không nhắc chuyện du khách ăn trộm máy.
